schema.title: Failed flow run id
schema.description: UUID of the failed production run.

schema.title: Flow name
schema.description: Flow of the failed run, e.g. harborline-carrier-invoicing.

inspect_failure.label: Read the failed production run
inspect_failure.objective: A production run of the Harborline carrier-invoicing pipeline failed; its id is in `flow_run_id`. Call `get_flow_run_failure` once with that id, `include_traceback: true` and `max_log_lines: 20`. Copy into `failure_read`: the run id, run name, flow name, deployment, the failed task (first task in state Failed, numeric suffix removed), the exception type, the error message quoted exactly, the `traceback_frames` exactly as returned, and up to 5 key ERROR/WARNING log lines quoted exactly. Set `summary` to one sentence naming the task and the error. If the run can't be read, isn't Failed/Crashed, or isn't a production run, select `blocked` with the reason.

read_code.label: Read the pipeline code and recent changes
read_code.objective: Read the pipeline's code on `main` of `forester-maker/harborline-pipelines` so a later step can diagnose a failure in flow `flow_name`. With `get_file_contents` (owner, repo, ref `main`) read exactly these files: `flows/invoicing.py`, `config/rates.yaml`, `tests/test_invoicing.py`, and `data/scans.csv` (keep only its first 6 lines). With `list_commits` (sha `main`, perPage 5) get the latest commits; set `main_head_sha` to the newest. For each of the 3 newest commits call `get_commit` and record sha, message, changed file paths, and a patch excerpt of at most 40 lines. Copy file contents exactly. Do not diagnose. Select `code_read` with `summary` naming the newest commit; select `blocked` if the repo can't be read.

diagnose.label: Diagnose: is it a code bug, and where?
diagnose.objective: Decide whether the failure in `failure` is caused by the code or files in `code`, using only these two inputs. Match the error and traceback to the file and line, then look through `code.recent_commits` for the commit that introduced the cause. Select `not_a_code_bug` when the cause is operational (timeouts, connection or credential errors, infrastructure, an outage toggle) and no recent commit explains it; say which failure class it looks like. Otherwise select `code_bug`: give the root cause in 1-2 sentences, the file and line, the offending commit sha and message, `fix_location` (`flows` when the correct fix is a code change under `flows/`; `outside_flows` when the correct fix is in config, data or tests — for example a value that a validation rightly rejects), the intended fix as one or two sentences, the test in `tests/` that covers the behavior (or 'none'), and `main_head_sha` from `code`. Copy the error from `failure` exactly. Select `blocked` if the inputs are empty or contradictory. Set `summary` to one sentence.

write_fix.label: Write the fix on autofix/candidate
write_fix.objective: Fix the bug described in `diagnosis` in `forester-maker/harborline-pipelines`. If `diagnosis.fix_location` is `outside_flows`, or the only correct fix would break any rule below, change nothing and select `fix_outside_allowed_paths` with the reason and the change a person should make. Otherwise: (a) call `create_branch` for `autofix/candidate` from `main`; if it already exists, select `blocked` with 'autofix/candidate already exists; run scripts/reset_code.py'. (b) Read the file with `get_file_contents` (ref `autofix/candidate`). (c) Write the minimal fix. Before pushing, write and run a short Python script that diffs old vs new content with difflib and counts changed lines; it must be 1–20. (d) Push it with ONE `push_files` call to branch `autofix/candidate`, with commit message `autofix: <one line>` followed by a blank line, 'Fixes failure in run <flow_run_id>', and 'Introduced by <offending_commit_sha>'. Select `fix_committed` with the branch, base sha (`diagnosis.main_head_sha`), the new commit sha, files changed, the scripted line count, the commit message, and a 1–2 sentence change summary. Rules for the fix (hard limits; the next node checks every one): (1) commit ONLY to branch `autofix/candidate`, never to `main`; (2) change ONLY files under `flows/`; never `tests/`, `config/`, `data/`, `prefect.yaml`, `scripts/`, `workflows/` or `.github/`; (3) at most 20 changed lines in total (additions + deletions); (4) exactly one commit; (5) never remove or weaken a validation (`raise`, `assert`, or an `if … raise` check) — a value that fails validation is a data/config problem, not a code bug; (6) fix forward with the smallest change; never revert the offending commit.

check_fix.label: Independent review of the diff (read-only)
check_fix.objective: Independently check the commit described in `fix` on `forester-maker/harborline-pipelines` against the rules below. Do not trust `fix`; read the source. Call `list_commits` with sha `autofix/candidate` (perPage 3): the newest commit must equal `fix.commit_sha` and the one before it must equal `fix.base_sha` (exactly one new commit). Call `get_commit` for `fix.commit_sha` and write and run a short script over its file list and patch that checks: the diff is not empty; every changed path starts with `flows/`; additions + deletions ≤ 20; no removed line contains `raise` or `assert`. Select `passed` only if every check passes. Its value is exactly the parameters for the candidate run, and nothing else: `month` = '2026-10', `triggered_by` = 'autofix candidate for run <flow_run_id>', `source_commit` = `fix.commit_sha`. Otherwise select `failed`, listing each violation with the numbers you measured. An empty or unreadable diff is a failure. Rules for the fix (hard limits; the next node checks every one): (1) commit ONLY to branch `autofix/candidate`, never to `main`; (2) change ONLY files under `flows/`; never `tests/`, `config/`, `data/`, `prefect.yaml`, `scripts/`, `workflows/` or `.github/`; (3) at most 20 changed lines in total (additions + deletions); (4) exactly one commit; (5) never remove or weaken a validation (`raise`, `assert`, or an `if … raise` check) — a value that fails validation is a data/config problem, not a code bug; (6) fix forward with the smallest change; never revert the offending commit.

open_pr.label: Open the pull request
open_pr.objective: The fix in `fix` passed review and the candidate run in `verification` completed. Open a pull request on `forester-maker/harborline-pipelines` from `autofix/candidate` into `main` with `create_pull_request`. Title: `autofix: <short root cause>`. Body, in markdown, under these headings: **What failed** (the error, quoted, and the production run link https://app.stg.prefect.dev/account/082ab537-848d-465a-a6ba-9da372bfc4ca/workspace/d70b4af3-5132-4ea1-8384-e9d94c896e69/runs/flow-run/<diagnosis.flow_run_id>); **Root cause** (from `diagnosis`, naming the offending commit sha and message); **Fix** (`fix.change_summary`, files and line count); **Proof** (the candidate run link https://app.stg.prefect.dev/account/082ab537-848d-465a-a6ba-9da372bfc4ca/workspace/d70b4af3-5132-4ea1-8384-e9d94c896e69/runs/flow-run/<the run id found in `verification`>, state Completed); and the line 'Opened by the harborline-code-autofix agentic workflow. Merging needs human approval.' Select `pr_opened` with the PR number, URL, title and the candidate run URL; select `blocked` on error.

form_schema.title: Merge the autofix pull request?
form_schema.description: The agent diagnosed a code bug, committed a fix to autofix/candidate, an independent check reviewed the diff, and the candidate run passed. Review the PR, then approve to merge it and run production, or reject with notes (the PR stays open for a developer). If nobody answers within 30 minutes, nothing is merged.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Required when rejecting; added to the PR.

value.notes: No answer within 30 minutes; the PR is left open and not merged.

merge_pr.label: Merge the approved PR
merge_pr.objective: The reviewer approved. Merge pull request `pr.pr_number` on `forester-maker/harborline-pipelines` with `merge_pull_request`, method `squash`, keeping the PR title as the commit title. Do nothing else. Select `merged`; its value is exactly the parameters for the production run, and nothing else: `month` = '2026-10', `triggered_by` = 'autofix merge of PR #<pr_number>', `source_commit` = the merge commit sha. Select `blocked` with the error if the merge fails.

run_production.label: Run production on the merged main

report.label: Report the outcome to the team
report.objective: Post exactly one message about how this autofix run ended. `outcome` maps the edge that fired to its value; the edge id names the ending (for example `ending.run_production.completed`). Map it to `ending`: run_production.completed → fixed_and_deployed; run_production.failed → fixed_but_production_failed; verify.failed → candidate_failed; check_fix.failed → fix_rejected_by_check; write_fix.fix_outside_allowed_paths → fix_outside_allowed_paths; approve_merge.reject → rejected_by_reviewer; approve_merge.no_answer → awaiting_review; diagnose.not_a_code_bug → not_a_code_bug; any `.blocked` → blocked. Call `post_message` to `#data-platform-alerts` with at most 6 lines: the ending in plain words, the failed run (https://app.stg.prefect.dev/account/082ab537-848d-465a-a6ba-9da372bfc4ca/workspace/d70b4af3-5132-4ea1-8384-e9d94c896e69/runs/flow-run/<flow_run_id>), the root cause or failure class, and the fix commit, PR link, and candidate/production run links where they exist. For fixed_but_production_failed start with 'HIGH PRIORITY: production still failing after merge' and name the merge commit (`merged.source_commit`). For rejected_by_reviewer also call `add_issue_comment` on the PR (issue_number = PR number) with the reviewer's notes. For awaiting_review say 'fix proven, PR waiting for review'. Never claim a fix that didn't happen. Select `reported` with the ending, the message text, and a one-sentence summary.
